name: Percentage Calculator
description: Calculate a percentage of a number, what percent one number is of another, or the percent change between two numbers — three calculators in one, updating live.

faq.question: Why does a 20% increase then a 20% decrease not return the original number?
faq.answer: Because each percentage is calculated on a different base. Increasing 50 by 20% gives 60; decreasing 60 by 20% gives 48, not 50 — the second 20% is 20% of the larger number. This is a very common source of confusion, and exactly why the "% change" calculator here always shows the actual result rather than assuming it.

faq.question: What's the difference between the second and third calculators?
faq.answer: "X is what % of Y" answers a static question about proportion (10 out of 50 is 20%). "% change from X to Y" answers a question about growth or shrinkage between two values over time or between two states (going from 50 to 65 is a 30% increase) — the two calculations use the same numbers differently and aren't interchangeable.
